## Description

A vast circular chamber with pale light that seems to come from everywhere and nowhere. The walls are lined with doors — all identical, all locked except one. The air hums at a frequency you feel in your teeth more than hear.

## Atmosphere

The silence is absolute — not quiet, but the absence of sound. The pale light creates no shadows. Every footstep echoes wrong, too clean, too measured. The hum in the air is just below hearing, felt in the teeth and the base of the skull. The room feels like a held breath.

## Image System

The doors — all identical, all locked. The single open door, always the same one, always at the far end. The pale sourceless light. The hum. The circular symmetry that makes every direction feel the same.

## History

The Central Room was the original control hub of the Institute, where scientists monitored the developing consciousness simulations. When the program was sealed, the scientists removed themselves from the system but left the room intact — a relic that became, to the children, something between a temple and a prison.

## Dramatic Function

The Central Room is the testing ground. Every major revelation, every moment of doubt, every choice the children make happens here. It's where hope is given and taken away. The locked doors are the promise: there's something beyond. The single open door is the lie: only one path is permitted.
